`run_labs.py --unit S7`: PASS (26/26). The twin is byte-identical, runs under -I -W error with no stderr, and its output matches the page. No RNG, imports numpy only, 0.6 s in Pyodide. The hypothesis is demonstrated (recomputed in proj-number-lab-claims). The annotated reason for the stable sort is wrong. The code comment says 'stable: ties keep input order, so results are reproducible' and the interpretation says 'A stable sort makes ties reproducible'. (i) The BH mask does not depend on the order of ties: if p_(k) = p_(k+1) and k passes, then p_(k+1) = p_(k) <= kq/m < (k+1)q/m, so k+1 passes too, ties never straddle k*, and the rejected set {i : p_i <= p_(k*)} is order-free. (ii) NumPy's default argsort is deterministic anyway. In a worked example whose purpose is the 'why' of each line, this teaches a false necessity.
rows.fix: Replace the comment with '# any sort order gives the same mask: ties never straddle k* (if p_(k) = p_(k+1) passes at k it passes at k+1)', and the interpretation sentence with 'Ties cannot straddle k*: if p_(k) = p_(k+1) and k passes its line, so does k + 1, so the mask is the same for any sort order.' Questions I would have had to ask before starting. (1) Must benjamini_hochberg raise ValueError for a 2-D pvalues array? The contract states no dimensionality, but test_bh_input_validation[bad3] requires it. (2) Must sharpe_ratio, and the other series functions, raise for 2-D input? The contract says only 'a series r'; test_sharpe_ratio_rejects_degenerate_input[bad3] requires it. (3) What is the CSCV metric when a half-sample has one row? This happens for S = 2 with T in {2, 3}, which '2 <= S <= T' allows, and std(ddof=1) is undefined there; the reference then emits a NumPy RuntimeWarning (scripts/edge_cases.py). (4) What is t*_bk in romano_wolf when a resampled column has zero sample variance? The contract is silent; the reference substitutes np.finfo(float64).tiny.
